item.title: Nasdaq crashes 1,200 pts at close, erasing 2026 gains; S&P 500, Dow enter correction
item.description: US stocks experienced a steep selloff, leading to significant losses for major indexes like the S&P 500 and Dow. The selloff marked the biggest weekly declines since April 2025, confirming corrections for both indexes. Investor sentiment surrounding technology and AI stocks remains negative despite strong corporate earnings results. The Federal Reserve's potential interest rate increase continues to influence market expectations and trader strategies.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: US stocks extended their steep selloff on Friday, pushing the S&P 500 and the Dow into correction territory as Anthropic’s blockbuster listing failed to restore confidence in an artificial intelligence trade that had powered much of this year’s rally, Reuters reported.The S&P 500 dropped 257.38 points, or 3.59%, to 6,918.45. The Nasdaq Composite plunged 1,225.05 points, or 5.13%, to 22,654.15, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 908.88 points, or 1.85%, to 48,188.18.All three major indexes closed sharply lower and recorded their biggest weekly percentage declines since April 2025, when President Donald Trump announced his market-rattling “Liberation Day” tariffs.The S&P 500 and the Dow ended more than 10% below their record closing highs, confirming that both had entered corrections. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite erased its gains for the year.The S&P 500 fell for a seventh consecutive session, marking its longest losing streak since February 2020.For live updates on US Markets, click here“This is clearly a challenging day for capital markets, and as we head into a Friday close, it appears to be accelerating to a certain degree,” Bill Northey, senior investment director at US Bank Wealth Management, told Reuters.“When we step back and evaluate fundamentals and sentiment, sentiment is clearly winning the day,” Northey added. “Sentiment is always the more powerful force in the immediate term, whereas fundamentals tend to win out over time.”Strong corporate earnings and a resilient economy offered little support as investors continued to retreat from technology and AI-linked stocks.Anthropic’s highly anticipated initial public offering had been viewed as a potential turning point for the battered AI trade. The shares closed 17.1% above their $83 offer price on Thursday but surrendered much of their early surge as enthusiasm faded during the session. The stock then posted a steep decline on its second day of trading.The IPO, together with Nvidia’s quarterly earnings report, failed to ease concerns about stretched valuations and the enormous sums being invested in AI infrastructure.“Nvidia reported what might have been one of the greatest quarters in corporate earnings history; they did everything right,” said Chuck Carlson, chief executive officer at Horizon Investment Services, as per Reuters' report.“A lot of people, myself included, were looking to the Anthropic debut to some extent as a clearing event, and it wasn’t.”The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which had been a major driver of the broader market’s advance, tumbled as the once-crowded chip trade continued to unwind.Amazon and Meta Platforms were among the hyperscalers that suffered heavy losses, while AI cloud-computing companies CoreWeave and Nebius also fell sharply.The technology rout encouraged investors to move into traditionally defensive areas, including consumer staples and healthcare.Inflation and Fed policy in focusFederal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said the central bank’s policy rate was not sufficiently high to address elevated inflation.Traders were pricing in a near-certain 25-basis-point interest-rate increase at the Fed’s December meeting, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool.A University of Michigan survey showed an improvement in consumer sentiment following the election.Investors will turn next week to the personal consumption expenditures report, which includes the Fed’s preferred inflation measure, for further guidance on monetary policy after October inflation exceeded expectations.Among individual stocks, Intuit fell after lowering its annual revenue-growth forecast and agreeing to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion. Intuit acquired the business five years ago for nearly three times that amount.UnitedHealth Group advanced after TD Cowen upgraded the health insurer to “buy” from “hold.”Caterpillar declined as the retreat in AI-related shares raised concerns about demand for its power-generation and backup-power equipment.Bitcoin fell below $60,000, dragging down cryptocurrency-linked companies including Coinbase, Strategy and Robinhood.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)
